channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] EU seeks ways to make expansion more palatable to members
item.description: The European Commission has put forward ideas it hopes will both ease the EU expansion process and allay concerns among existing members. Several countries, not least war-torn Ukraine, are among the candidates.

item.title: [DW] France’s conundrum: How to cut spending amid protests
item.description: Prime Minister Lecornu is pledging to improve schools at a time when the government seeks to save billions. France's dilemma can be seen across the EU: How to cut spending when citizens are demanding more from the state?

item.title: [DW] Fact check: Misleading claims spark plague fears in Russia
item.description: The death of a lab worker at a plague research institute in Russia has sparked claims about a lab accident, hundreds of infections and international spread. Some of these viral narratives are misleading.

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump says he will speak with Putin about pneumonic plague
item.description: Washington increases pressure on Moscow to share more about the incident in which one person has died

item.title: [Financial Times] SpaceX looks to raise $40bn to buy Nvidia chips in financing led by Apollo
item.description: Blockbuster debt deal is the latest sign of the vast spending on chips and other infrastructure underpinning AI

item.title: [Politico Europe] Latvia moves to expel Russian journalist who used to work for BBC
item.description: Leonid Ragozin made remarks widely interpreted as making excuses for the Kremlin’s invasion of Ukraine and hybrid attacks in Europe.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Read the charter for the White House’s ‘Super Intelligence Force’
item.description: The new group has broad authority to determine how the government should protect against artificial intelligence threats.

item.title: [Financial Times] Jim Clyburn urges Black voters not to be ‘fooled’ by Trump
item.description: Civil rights veteran says Republicans will ‘reap the reaction’ for redistricting moves ahead of midterm elections

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump says he is considering suspending federal petrol tax
item.description: Surging fuel prices are heaping pressure on the president and his Republican Party four weeks ahead of midterm elections

item.title: [Financial Times] ‘Most dangerous product in crypto’ vexes Singapore
item.description: City-state averse to risk and scandal tries to distance itself from homegrown Hyperliquid Labs and its popular ‘perps’

item.title: [Financial Times] S&P 500 hits record high as AI stocks shrug off bond market slump
item.description: Wall Street’s benchmark index closes at fresh peak but rally is increasingly reliant on handful of tech stocks

item.title: [Politico Europe] Greens promise ‘campaign mode’ and continuity under new leaders
item.description: The Greens are pitching their new leadership as a reset ahead of 2029's European elections.

item.title: [Financial Times] Ships’ captains paid $100,000 a month to transit Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Salaries and bonuses spiral for seafarers willing to risk perilous trip through waterway in face of Iranian attacks

item.title: [Financial Times] Goldman Sachs and Man Group exposed in EY data breach
item.description: Disclosures widen the circle of victims of a hacking incident earlier this year

item.title: [EU Observer] Commission seeks 15-year safeguards on future member states, but says reforms won’t create two-tier EU
item.description: A proposed safeguard to last up to 15 years after EU accession would make it easier to suspend future member states' voting rights if they misbehaved.

item.title: [EU Observer] How bad does it have to get for the ECB to save France?
item.description: France is no Greece. A full-blown debt crisis is not yet on the cards. But as things stand, a protracted muddling through seems the most likely outcome.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Les renforts d’Europol en IA suscitent des inquiétudes sur la protection de la vie privée
item.description: L’agence européenne de coopération des services de police devra faire face à la fois aux cybercriminels et aux défenseurs de la vie privée.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Marine Le Pen, le tournant de la rigueur ?
item.description: 140 milliards d’euros d’économies net sur 5 ans, une règle d’or budgétaire, le retour de la somme des dépenses publiques sous les 50% du PIB… Marine Le Pen a voulu faire la démonstration de son sérieux et de sa crédibilité en matière de gestion des finances publiques en présentant sa “trajectoire financière” lors d’une conférence […]

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs warn against EU rush to restarting funds for Hungary while corruption and plurality concerns remain
item.description: Hungary is starting to address the EU's concerns over the rule of law and judicial independence, and the EU seems tkeen to quickly resume frozen funding for Budapest.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Britain’s Tories really, really don’t want to team up with Farage. They might still have to.
item.description: The Reform UK leader is the butt of mockery and vitriol at the Conservatives' annual gathering in Birmingham. That could make a coalition near-impossible.

item.title: [EU Observer] Von der Leyen joins MEPs in defence of EU’s €2 trillion spending plan ahead of summit
item.description: “I would like to caution against large cuts. It would risk cutting deep into critical priorities that we all together have agreed on,” the EU Commission chief told MEPs during a speech in Strasbourg on Tuesday.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ireland’s 2027 budget offers tax break to help people invest savings
item.description: The Irish are hoping to woo some of the €170 billion sitting in low-interest deposit accounts into riskier investments with higher returns.

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘Accidents happen’: French PM defends police after teenagers injured in protests
item.description: Sébastien Lecornu vowed to offer a “political response” to French students' concerns after being accused of reacting to protests with force alone.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU needs to solve the cost-of-living crisis to stop far-right populists, Portuguese PM Luís Montenegro tells MEPs
item.description: Portuguese prime minister told MEPs that solving the cost of living crisis is key to keeping the far-right out of power, as ultra-nationalist party reaches record popularity at home.

item.title: [EU Observer] German ex-spy chief arrested over espionage and treason allegations involving leaked BND files
item.description: Germany’s former spy chief now stands accused of selling thousands of ultra-sensitive intelligence files to foreign clients, in a scandal insiders warn could cripple Berlin’s trust with allied services.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Greens probe conduct complaint against Deputy Leader Mothin Ali
item.description: Left-wing party looks at claim Mothin Ali "snatched" phone from fellow member in alleged Leeds altercation.

item.title: [EU Observer] The children of Gaza are being killed every day. Where are the headlines?
item.description: EU governments continue to authorise arms sales to Israel despite rules and the EU treaties that require them to protect children's rights.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Jailed Albanian mayor uses AI avatar to make deepfake speech
item.description: The mayor of Tirana is behind bars but still running the city — with a bit of help from technology.

item.title: [EU Observer] AI machine-gun turrets do battle with Russian jet drones for the skies of Kyiv (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,685)
item.description: The battle for Kyiv's skies aside, Ukraine’s air raids on Russian oil sites saw it boast that over half of Moscow’s refinery capacity was offline, potentially choking fuel supplies far from the front.

item.title: [Financial Times] California’s oligarch tax would change America
item.description: The goal of its framers is political rather than budgetary

item.title: [EU Observer] Centre-right’s Muslim Brotherhood witch-hunt in EU Parliament risks criminalising everyday activism
item.description: If Brussels accepts this vague hunt for “Muslim Brotherhood networks”, the same logic could later be turned against almost any vocal minority in Europe.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Is the EU actually willing to speed up enlargement?
item.description: The EU wants to bring new countries on board faster. But after years of waiting, will the Commission’s new proposals actually make enlargement easier?

item.title: [Financial Times] Sleep has always been a class issue
item.description: There is still a class divide when it comes to work that tramples over your body clock

item.title: [DW] Latvians head to the polls with Russia on their minds
item.description: On October 3, Latvians will elect a new parliament with Russia looming large over the campaign. Security fears dominate the agenda, but so does a debate over the economic cost of cutting ties with Moscow.

item.title: [DW] Nationalists top Bosnia-Herzegovina's divisive election
item.description: Bosnia-Herzegovina's three-member presidency is set to be dominated by nationalists from the three major ethnic groups, including Zeljka ​Cvijanovic, backed by disqualified Serb secessionist leader Milorad Dodik.

item.title: [DW] UK remands 2 Iranians over alleged antisemitic terror plot
item.description: The pair were arrested on the eve of Yom Kippur and later charged with plotting to attack Jewish targets in Manchester.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia and Herzegovina is still shaped by war, separatism, EU ambitions
item.description: Bosnia and Herzegovina is governed by a system established after the Bosnian war — more than 30 years ago. Ethnic divisions, a complex administration and European integration all shape the country's political reality.

item.title: [DW] Merz, Macron seek tougher EU measures against unfair trade
item.description: Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz have written to Ursula von der Leyen, calling for tougher EU mechanisms against unfair trade practices by other states. They name no names but seem to have China or the US in mind.

item.title: [DW] Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
item.description: A worker at a plague research institute in Siberia has died, and nearly 200 of her contacts are under medical observation. Russian authorities deny a link to the bacterial infection. The US is monitoring the situation.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia election: New steps to prevent electoral fraud, but nationalist parties remain on top
item.description: New technology has stopped votes being cast on behalf of dead or absent voters, and turnout has fallen to a record low. But it was a case of deja vu in Bosnia's elections with the same parties winning.

item.title: [DW] Hundreds of French schools shut, teen loses hand in protests
item.description: The student protests that rocked France last week have prompted authorities to keep up to 500 schools closed on Monday. A teenage boy lost his hand, seemingly while trying to pick up a police tear gas grenade.

item.title: [EU Observer] Why ‘Made in Europe’ could push Burnham’s UK back into the EU’s arms
item.description: For UK Burnham, the growing risk of UK industry becoming collateral damage in an EU-China trade war is turning abstract talk of “better cooperation” into a stark choice between limited market fixes or a full-scale return to the EU table.

item.title: [EU Observer] Women MEPs targeted by AI ‘nudifier’ apps push EU leaders to enforce December ban
item.description: If a woman enters politics, she may have to confront the fact that she may be one in 14 being digitally stripped by 'nudifying' technology. Such is what an EU ban is trying to stop: but whether it will be implemented in time, according to the Parliament's greens party, is far from certain.

item.title: [EU Observer] Putin and Vučić dominate Bosnia elections, as EU fades out of view
item.description: Last elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina might prove that Russia's influence is more broadly spread than the EU's.

item.title: [EU Observer] Spain’s 54-day sprint to the polls: can Sánchez’s housing gamble stop the far-right from entering into government?
item.description: Spain's Pedro Sánchez has called snap elections for 29 November, after parliament rejected his housing decrees, giving him a hot-button political issue for his election platform. But polls favour the opposition centre-right People's Party, which may need the far-right Vox to govern. And the loss of Sánchez would be a big blow for the centre-left in Brussels.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘They want to shut me up’: Norwegian activist fights 20‑year Greek prison threat over asylum aid
item.description: Norwegian activist Tommy Olsen says he is facing enormous personal and financial costs over Greek allegations that he belongs to a criminal organisation, in a trial that starts on Tuesday in Rhodes.

item.title: [DW] Spain's parliament rejects housing bill as protests continue
item.description: Spain's minority government suffered defeat in parliament as it tried to push through a pair of emergency measures aimed at making housing more affordable. A pensioner's eviction and protests led to the bid.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine, South Korea clash over transfer of 2 North Korean prisoners
item.description: A diplomatic scandal has erupted over two North Korean prisoners of war, with South Korea demanding an apology from Ukraine. What's been the reaction in Kyiv?

item.title: [DW] Turkey: Stock market scandal hits half a million investors
item.description: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests, and a leading AKP lawmaker has resigned.

item.title: [DW] EU ministers mull new ways to curb irregular migration
item.description: The proposals include setting up so-called return hubs outside the EU and strengthening the border agency Frontex. Greece has even proposed temporarily suspending asylum applications in emergency situations.
